top.title: ‘It’s difficult to be positive’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 0-4 defeat
top.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has admitted that it is difficult to remain positive after his side suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. Pochettino, who was overseeing his first home match as United manager, expressed disappointment with the result but urged his players to remain united and work together to turn around the club’s fortunes. Speaking after the encounter at Old Trafford, the Argentine said United started the match strongly but struggled after conceding the opening goal. “Difficult to be positive. Very disappointed, disappointed at the same time because I feel sorry for the players,” he said. “The players from the beginning, during 15 to 20 minutes, we were very solid, organisation, structure. I think we were controlling the game. The moment we concede the goal, we should not concede this goal.” Callum Wilson scored twice in the first half to put Brentford in control before Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade added two more goals in the closing stages to complete the visitors’ victory. Pochettino admitted that conceding the first goal affected his players’ confidence and made the contest more difficult for them. He insisted that the squad must remain calm despite the difficult situation, adding that he believes the team will improve with time. “The game goes difficult, the intensity, the nerves. This situation, a situation like this, is affecting your confidence, but we need to be united and stay together and keep pushing. “We are going to push to improve and, of course, it is only a matter of time that we are going to improve. We need to stay together, we need to stay calm. That is why we’re here. We have the responsibility to turn this situation into another way,” he added. Asked whether the challenge at Manchester United had been bigger than he initially anticipated, Pochettino said he knew the club was going through difficult circumstances before accepting the job. The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager explained that the team’s busy fixture schedule had also made it difficult to implement his ideas, particularly with three matches played within 10 days. “No, we knew it was going to be bigger. That is why we are here. No change in my view. Only that things need time to change in football more. When the fixtures and schedule is so busy,” he said. He added that the players had remained receptive to his instructions and were making efforts to improve despite the disappointing results. “The reaction of the players when we lost 4-0. They tried and they care. That is the most important thing. We need to feel the pain and increase our standards and try to do anything to be much better.” The defeat extended United’s winless run in the Premier League to 10 matches, their longest such streak since going 11 games without a victory between November 1989 and February 1990. top.title: Who Phoenix Suns will play in added games from NBA Cup group results
top.description: The Phoenix Suns will play the Houston Rockets and Oklahoma City Thunder to complete their 82-game schedule after failing to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals. The Suns (9-9) face the Rockets (14-5) in Houston on Dec. 6 and face the Thunder (10-9) at home Dec. 10. Eight teams are set for the “knockout rounds” after the final group play games on Nov. 27. Dec. 4: East quarterfinal — (3) Philadelphia 76ers at (2) Atlanta Hawks; West quarterfinal — (4) San Antonio Spurs at (1) Dallas Mavericks . Dec. 5: East quarterfinal — (4) Boston Celtics at (1) Detroit Pistons ; West quarterfinal — (3) Memphis Grizzlies at (2) Portland Trail Blazers . The top three seeds won their respective groups, while the fourth seeds are wild cards in their respective conferences. The remaining 22 teams that didn’t advance must play two games amongst themselves to each have a full 82-game regular season. Here’s the NBA’s explanation on how those matchups were decided. “A formulaic approach will determine the matchups for these games using the group play standings in each conference (5th-15th). Two of the 22 games will be scheduled cross-conference since there will be an odd number of teams in each conference that do not advance to the quarterfinals. “These cross-conference games will be scheduled between bottom-finishing teams in the group play stage subject to travel constraints, and no team will play more than one of its two games cross-conference. The other 20 games will be scheduled within conference, featuring teams that are otherwise scheduled to play each other three times over the course of the season wherever possible.” The Suns and Rockets were in West Group A. Phoenix went 1-3 in group play while Houston finished 2-2 with one victory coming against the Suns on Nov. 25. Having already played each other twice this season, they will meet two more times on Dec. 6 and Feb. 5. Phoenix won the first matchup Nov. 7 at home. The teams have recent history that’s factored in intense, heated matchups. Phoenix traded Durant to Houston before the 2025 draft and got Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and the 10 th overall pick in the 2025 draft, 7-footer Khaman Maluach, in return. There were six technical fouls and one flagrant one penalty foul in the last meeting. Brooks was ejected after two technical fouls, with the second coming after he and Durant engaged in a spirited conversation face-to-face late in the game. The Suns and Thunder will now battle each other four times as well this season. Oklahoma City won the first game on Oct. 26. The final three Suns-Thunder matchups will be in Phoenix, as the final two are on a back-to-back March 23-24. Oklahoma City went 2-2 in West Group B. top.title: Robinson edges Shiffrin to win Killington giant slalom
top.description: New Zealand's Alice Robinson claimed victory in the women's World Cup giant slalom in Killington, Vermont (Maddie Meyer) Alice Robinson won the women's World Cup giant slalom on Saturday at Killington, where Mikaela Shiffrin settled for second in her return to the Vermont course where she was seriously injured in a 2024 crash. New Zealand's Robinson, second behind Shiffrin after the opening run, defied the poor visibility and deteriorating course conditions to triumph with a total time of 2min 03.02sec, 11-hundredths ahead of Shiffrin. The US superstar held on for second ahead of American teammate Paula Moltzan, who was on the podium again after capturing her first career World Cup win at the season-opening giant slalom in Soelden last month. Robinson, who was 39-hundredths behind Shiffrin after the opening run, bagged her seventh World Cup giant slalom win, her eighth World Cup race victory overall. Shiffrin, meanwhile, remained in search of a first giant slalom win in almost three years. Shiffrin was back at Killington, a two-hour drive from the Burke Mountain Academy she attended as a teenager, for the first time since a 2024 crash that left her with a serious abdominal injury. Shiffrin thrilled her home crowd as she stormed to the lead in the first leg. The 31-year-old American was clearly delighted also, punching a fist in celebration and blowing a kiss to the crowd. Shiffrin had returned to her top form in slalom last season, winning Olympic gold at the Milan-Cortina Winter Games and bagging a sixth overall World Cup title. But she struggled to overcome the psychological toll of her high-speed crash in Killington, in which she suffered a painful deep puncture wound. This year she has opted to focus more on giant slalom and super-G, and Sunday's slalom in Killington will be her first in that discipline this season. bb/nf

top.title: Quin Snyder, Dyson Daniels explain how Atlanta Hawks turned tables on Boston Celtics
top.description: For much of the Atlanta Hawks 87-86 NBA Cup win over the Boston Celtics at TD Garden this Friday (Nov. 27) evening, it seemed like Boston's defense was keeping Atlanta from hitting the broad side of a barn with their shot selection. "“I think sometimes if you’re not making shots, it deflates you a little bit, and that’s the right word," said Hawks head coach Quin Snyder. "I think it’s energy and we had a lot more urgency getting the ball in, more urgency running." "But again, sometimes when you’re missing, it’s hard to get back to the present and so even when we got stops, I didn’t think we were quite as urgent to run," he added. "And eventually, something we talked about at halftime, trying to really take advantage of our defense and we never really ended up hitting a lot of shots but we kept shooting and we made some timely ones." "The other thing (was) we weren’t running and we stopped rebounding, but we did defensive rebound," continued the Atlanta coach. Things, however, changed in the third quarter for the Hawks, as Atlanta guard Dyson Daniels noted. "“I just thought everyone sat down and guarded the ball," he recalled. "Our gameplan tonight was to come in, it was going to be a lot less help because of the spacing on the floor. So, let’s sit down and guard the ball, and I thought we did that very well tonight. Everyone came in and really guarded, which was fun." Listen to "Airing Boston Celtics grievances, and feats of strength to fix them" on Spreaker. top.title: 12x possession lost, 75% duels lost, 0 crosses: Joshua Zirkzee failed to make rare chance count; he let Pochettino down v Brentford
top.description: 12x possession lost, 75% duels lost, 0 crosses: Joshua Zirkzee failed to make rare chance count; he let Pochettino down v Brentford Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Brentford on Saturday, the third consecutive Premier League game in which the Red Devils have conceded four times. Senne Lammens was shocking yet again, and the defence keeps leaking goals even when the team is in control of the game. INEOS know that they need to bring in defensive reinforcements to help Mauricio Pochettino; otherwise things could get ugly really soon. But the new head coach’s decision to start with Patrick Dorgu, Amad and Joshua Zirkzee backfired spectacularly . Joshua Zirkzee struggles again The trio have never been known for their goalscoring prowess, and that was clearly on display on Saturday. United had 24 shots, but only six on target. The Dutchman , in particular, remains a mystery. His link-up play is great, and he can manipulate the ball in tight spaces, almost like a five-a-side baller. But when it comes to the sheer grit needed to get into the box or finish off chances, he remains an underperforming asset for the club. The 25-year-old looks much better when playing in Europe due to the slower tempo, but he struggles in the Premier League due to the sheer pace of the game in England. Off the ball, he is a liability This is especially apparent off the ball, with the former Bologna ace losing possession 12 times. And despite his physical frame, he is lightweight when it comes to protecting the ball. The Netherlands international won only two duels out of eight (aerial and ground combined). He also did not complete a single tackle. J. Zirkzee vs Brentford Page 1 of 2 1 2 And he produced one key pass while completing two dribbles (all stats via Sofascore ). That is simply not good enough for a United striker leading the line. Time for a new striker to come in He was handed a rare chance to start a league game and he let the boss down. Talks of an impending exit will surely ramp up in the coming weeks. No wonder Pochettino needs another striker in Benjamin Sesko’s absence. Until then, he should start his heavy hitters like Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha moving forward.

top.title: 'The better team won' - Frank Lampard admits Coventry were outclassed by Leeds after 3-0 defeat on return to Elland Road
top.description: Leeds United v Coventry City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Frank Lampard admitted "the better team won" after Coventry were beaten 3-0 by Leeds at Elland Road on Saturday, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and a Sean Longstaff double sinking his side. The Sky Blues boss was frustrated by the way his team conceded, but insisted the result will not define their season and turned his attention to Tuesday's visit of Ipswich. Lampard concedes Leeds were superior Lampard admitted "the better team won" after Coventry were beaten 3-0 by Leeds at Elland Road. Speaking to BBC Match of the Day , he said: "The better team won, that was clear. The positive is we haven't played like that much this season, maybe Arsenal in the first game." Calvert-Lewin, who recently signed a new contract , opened the scoring five minutes before half-time, and Longstaff added a second on the stroke of the interval before wrapping up the win midway through the second half. The result lifted Leeds to sixth, while Coventry are just three points above the relegation zone. Coventry boss frustrated by sloppy goals "In recent games we have shown a real competition and energy and today is one where we fell below that and Leeds were on it and are a very good team," Lampard continued. He added: "Both goals [in the first half] were disappointing from our point of view, you can't allow Dominic Calvert-Lewin the freedom to stroll in like that. To come here and get on top is not easy. It's disappointing but I know how much the boys are giving. Leeds have been in this league for a couple of years and are in a different phase." Away form a growing concern The defeat was a painful return to Elland Road for Lampard, whose Derby side famously knocked Leeds out of the Championship play-off semi-finals in 2019 after the Spygate scandal. Coventry have now won just one of their six away league games this season, against Nottingham Forest. However, Lampard insisted the setback would not derail the newly promoted side. "These games can happen, will they define our season? No. But the reaction in games coming up is important and it's important we learn from it," he said. Ipswich clash now crucial Coventry return to the CBS Arena on Tuesday to face Ipswich, and Lampard knows the importance of that fixture. "The next one against Ipswich, those are the games that will define our season," he said.

top.title: Ball hails Torquay endeavour in Chelmsford draw
top.description: Jimmy Ball's side have not lost a league game since 31 October [Shutterstock] Torquay United manager Jimmy Ball says he could not believe his side did not beat Chelmsford City in National League South. The Gulls missed a host of chances as they drew 1-1 with their opponents, who dropped out of the play-off zone as a result. The point saw the Gulls move up a place to 11th and are four points off the play-off places. Deon Moore gave Torquay a 15th-minute lead as he converted Jacob Beaumont-Clark's pass. Beaumont-Clark hit the post 10 minutes later and then hit the crossbar before Jack Roles headed in a 41st-minute equaliser. Torquay continued to create chances after the break as Moore went close and Sonny-Blu Lo-Everton had an effort cleared off the line with 10 minutes left. "I don't know how we've not won a game of football if I'm being honest, I really don't," Ball told BBC Radio Devon. "No one's going to be asking me for my lottery numbers I don't think. "But what was really pleasing is the fans seemed to appreciate what we've done out there. "I know we haven't won a game for them and I'm so desperate to, but I don't know what more we can do there today and on another day we do. "It's a really tough one to take, but we're unbeaten in five now, and so I keep saying green shoots don't I. When are they going to become trees? "The lads are gutted because they've given so much and the performance was fantastic. "If that's their level and they can perform to that level week in, week out between now and the end of the season we'll be just fine." Related internet links Torquay United

top.title: Bears get positive news on Colston Loveland after scary Thanksgiving injury
top.description: The Chicago Bears have received encouraging news about tight end Colston Loveland after his frightening knee injury against the Detroit Lions. A second medical opinion suggests Loveland could avoid injured reserve and return later this NFL season. ESPN NFL analyst Adam Schefter shared the latest update on X. “A second opinion on Bears TE Colston Loveland’s sprained MCL showed that he now is expected to avoid being placed on injured reserve, and the team is considering him week to week, per source.” MORE: Biggest winners & losers from NFL Thanksgiving Week games A second opinion on Bears TE Colston Loveland’s sprained MCL showed that he now is expected to avoid being placed on injured reserve, and the team is considering him week to week, per source. pic.twitter.com/wua1ra9QYa — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 28, 2026 Loveland injured his left knee during Thursday’s 39-35 Thanksgiving victory over Detroit. The incident happened in the first quarter while he blocked on a D’Andre Swift running play. Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez rolled into Loveland’s leg from behind. The tight end left the field with assistance and was quickly ruled out. Colston Loveland’s absence could test Chicago’s offense Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions defensive end Derrick Moore (8) knocks the ball away from Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland (84) at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Avoiding injured reserve represents an important development for Chicago. An IR placement would have required Loveland to miss at least four games. The tight end has recorded 41 receptions for 397 yards and three touchdowns across 11 starts. He ranks third on the team in receiving yards and remains an important target for quarterback Caleb Williams. However, Chicago already faces a major depth problem at tight end. Veteran Cole Kmet suffered a season-ending ACL injury in Week 7, leaving Loveland with increased responsibilities. Rookie Sam Roush and veteran Stephen Carlson could now handle larger roles. The pair combined for seven receptions and 61 yards against Detroit. The Bears sit atop the NFC North and have built a strong position for the playoff race. Their next challenge comes against the Jacksonville Jaguars. top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect BRIGHTON – Bad news for the Boston Bruins , but at the same time, some good news is coming soon. After practice on Saturday morning, Marco Sturm announced that Bruins captain David Pastrnak will be “day-to-day” with a non-contact, lower-body injury sustained in the first period on Friday. Pastrnak was in pain after taking several strides in the defensive zone and left the game after 5:50 TOI. Pastrnak did not practice on Saturday and will not play on Sunday against the Vancouver Canucks. “So he’s day-to-day,” Sturm said of Pastrnak. “He’ll definitely be out tomorrow, and we are going to reassess on Monday.” Sturm: David Pastrnak is out “day-to-day” with a lower-body injury “There’s a good chance” James Hagens will play tomorrow against Vancouver. @BOSHockeyNow | #NHLBruins pic.twitter.com/Xt5YoU2Sff — Jack Studley (@jackstudley13) November 28, 2026 The Bruins, without their best player, did not beat Anthony Stolarz in a 3-1 loss to the Maple Leafs on Friday. Marco Sturm moved JJ Peterka to the top power play, which remained intact on Saturday, and the first line looks slightly different, with Peterka and Morgan Geekie on the wings. Aside from being the Bruins’ best player, Pastrnak dons the captain’s ‘C.’ It’s his first year wearing the new letter, as last year the Bruins opted for a triumvirate of alternate captains. That transition shouldn’t be too hard on Charlie McAvoy and Tanner Jeannot, who both wear the alternate’s ‘A’ this season. “I don’t really have to talk to them,” Sturm said of Jeannot and McAvoy. “We always said, so the captain is out, Charlie will probably be the next guy up talking to the refs and making sure everything, even in the room, everything is under control. He’s used to this. He did it all last year. He did it in the past, too. So for me, it’s not a big worry. But the thing is, too, when David is out, that means there’s Zadorov and the Lindholms and all the other guys, Jeannot, they got to make sure we all step up as a unit.” Read Next David Pastrnak Exits Bruins’ Game With Non-Contact Injury James Hagens Nearing Return, Reunites With Old Linemates It’s not just going to be the alternate captains that step up in Pastrnak’s absence. Pastrnak leads the Bruins with 32 points (11-21–32), and the next closest is Elias Lindholm’s 22 (11-11–22). Lindholm found success alongside Casey Mittelstadt and James Hagens earlier this season, but that line was separated with Hagens’ injury. The line reunited on Saturday. “Yeah, I think everybody’s just got to give their best. It’s tough when your top guy goes out,” James Hagens said after practice. “All these guys in the room are going to be able to step up. We’re going to have each other’s backs out there and be ready to go.” Hagens skated in a white sweater, signaling a move to the top-six forward group. The Orlando Magic could be without guard Anthony Black as they prepare to open their four-game road trip against the Washington Wizards on Saturday. The Magic’s latest injury report, released at noon Saturday, listed the 22-year-old as questionable with back soreness. Orlando (7-10) will look to snap its two-game losing streak against Washington (7-12), with tipoff scheduled for 5 p.m. ET. Black last appeared in Orlando’s 104-86 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday, enduring a difficult offensive outing. The fourth-year guard finished with five points, four rebounds, two assists and one block while committing five turnovers across 28 minutes. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He shot 2-for-8 from the field, missed both of his 3-point attempts and went 1-for-3 from the free-throw line. Despite his struggles against Detroit, Black has continued to establish himself as a significant contributor for Orlando throughout the opening weeks of the 2026-27 season. Through 14 appearances, including 13 starts, Black is averaging 15.3 points, 5.1 assists, five rebounds and 1.8 steals per game while shooting 43.1% from the field and 39.1% from 3-point range in 32.7 minutes per contest. Anthony Black’s injury status looms large as Magic seek first win over Wizards Black’s uncertain availability comes as Orlando looks to avoid a third consecutive loss against Washington this season. The Magic suffered a 116-96 defeat against the Wizards last Sunday, marking their second double-digit loss to Washington this month. Orlando previously fell 103-94 to the Wizards on Nov. 2. Both teams enter Saturday’s matchup looking to improve their position in the Eastern Conference standings following inconsistent starts to the regular season. For first-year head coach Sean Sweeney, Black’s potential absence would present another challenge for an Orlando team that has dealt with several injuries throughout the season. His versatility as a ball-handler, perimeter defender and secondary scoring option has made him an important component of the Magic’s rotation. Saturday’s contest also presents Orlando with an opportunity to establish momentum at the beginning of an extended stretch away from home. As for whether Black will play against Washington, his questionable designation leaves his availability uncertain heading into Saturday’s matchup, with a final decision expected closer to tipoff.

top.title: Why your range game doesn't translate to the course
top.description: Hitting the same club at the same target feels great, but it rarely holds up. Getty Images You take a lesson on a Tuesday afternoon. With your coach watching, your swing feels smooth and crisp, and you hit 40 pure iron shots in a row. You walk off the practice tee convinced you’ve finally figured out this game. On Saturday morning, you stand on the first tee of your club tournament. There’s a pond down the right side and a group watching from behind the tee. You swing and hit a weak push-slice straight into the water. By the 14th hole, you’re searching for whatever swing thought you had on Tuesday. Golfers tell me some version of this story all the time. The problem isn’t talent or mental toughness. It’s that most golfers practice in a way that looks very little like playing golf. On the range, you hit ball after ball with the same club to the same target. On the course, you get one chance with a different club, to a different target, often after a five-minute wait, with real consequences. Why you struggle on the course Motor-learning researchers measure skill development in two ways: retention and transfer. Retention is the ability to reproduce a skill after a break under the same conditions in which you practiced it. Hit crisp 8-irons off a flat mat on Tuesday, come back Thursday and do it again, and you’ve demonstrated retention. Transfer is the ability to take that skill and apply it somewhere new: an uneven lie in the rough, a penalty area down the right, a crosswind and a score that counts. The golf course is the ultimate test of transfer. Yet most golfers spend nearly all their practice time working on retention. Hit the same club to the same target over and over, and the task becomes artificially easy. Your first shot pushes slightly right. On the second, your brain makes a quick adjustment. By the fourth, you’ve started to dial in the timing for that particular club and target. Before long, the shots look effortless. You leave believing you’ve mastered your 8-iron, but what you’ve really done is calibrate your timing through repetition. On the course, you never hit 15 8-irons in a row. You hit a driver, walk for five minutes, find your ball, pull an 8-iron, and face a shot over a bunker. And you get one chance to execute it. When you change clubs and targets with every swing, you can’t rely on the feel of the previous shot. Each ball requires a fresh decision: Read the target, choose the club, visualize the flight and commit. Motor-learning researchers call the added challenge of switching between tasks contextual interference . It tends to make practice look less successful in the moment, but the skills you develop are more likely to hold up when conditions change. top.title: Last Man Standing? Bayern Munich might only have one attacker left healthy
top.description: (Photo by Christina Pahnke - sampics/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich’s injury crisis has officially reached the point of absurdity. What was already a concerning list of absences has become a full-blown attacking personnel disaster, with virtually every major attacking option either sidelined or dealing with fitness concerns. After the latest setbacks against Hamburger SV, Bayern is staring at a situation where they barely have enough healthy attackers to put together a functional front line — and even the one player available is likely still working his way back to full fitness. Bayern currently have ONE fit first-team attacker: Kane ❌ Olise ❌ Musiala ❌ Díaz ✅ Saibari ❌ Gnabry ❌ Karl ❌ — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) November 28, 2026 Luis Díaz is essentially the last man standing, and he is coming off a spell on the sidelines himself. That is the attacking situation Bayern Munich are staring at right now, and it is difficult to overstate just how absurd this injury crisis has become. At some point, this stops being about rotation, squad management, or finding the perfect tactical adjustment. There is only so much Vincent Kompany can do when nearly his entire attacking arsenal is unavailable, yet that does not make the situation any less alarming — particularly with the Champions League and Bundesliga demanding results. Bayern cannot reasonably expect to navigate this stretch of the season by asking Díaz to carry the entire attack while patching together lineups with midfielders, youngsters, and whoever is medically cleared to lace up their boots. The January transfer window is no longer a conversation about luxury additions or opportunistic deals. It has become a conversation about survival, squad depth, and whether Bayern Munich can afford to keep pretending this situation will magically resolve itself. This is beyond frustrating. It should be noted, however, that Kompany did not acknowledge an injury to Karl. Hopefully, there is some silver lining there and the youngster is not actually hurt. nigeria.title: ‘It’s difficult to be positive’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 0-4 defeat
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has admitted that it is difficult to remain positive after his side suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. Pochettino, who was overseeing his first home match as United manager, expressed disappointment with the result but urged his players to remain united and work together to turn around the club’s fortunes. Speaking after the encounter at Old Trafford, the Argentine said United started the match strongly but struggled after conceding the opening goal. “Difficult to be positive. Very disappointed, disappointed at the same time because I feel sorry for the players,” he said. “The players from the beginning, during 15 to 20 minutes, we were very solid, organisation, structure. I think we were controlling the game. The moment we concede the goal, we should not concede this goal.” Callum Wilson scored twice in the first half to put Brentford in control before Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade added two more goals in the closing stages to complete the visitors’ victory. Pochettino admitted that conceding the first goal affected his players’ confidence and made the contest more difficult for them. He insisted that the squad must remain calm despite the difficult situation, adding that he believes the team will improve with time. “The game goes difficult, the intensity, the nerves. This situation, a situation like this, is affecting your confidence, but we need to be united and stay together and keep pushing. “We are going to push to improve and, of course, it is only a matter of time that we are going to improve. We need to stay together, we need to stay calm. That is why we’re here. We have the responsibility to turn this situation into another way,” he added. Asked whether the challenge at Manchester United had been bigger than he initially anticipated, Pochettino said he knew the club was going through difficult circumstances before accepting the job. The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager explained that the team’s busy fixture schedule had also made it difficult to implement his ideas, particularly with three matches played within 10 days. “No, we knew it was going to be bigger. That is why we are here. No change in my view. Only that things need time to change in football more. When the fixtures and schedule is so busy,” he said. He added that the players had remained receptive to his instructions and were making efforts to improve despite the disappointing results. “The reaction of the players when we lost 4-0. They tried and they care. That is the most important thing. We need to feel the pain and increase our standards and try to do anything to be much better.” The defeat extended United’s winless run in the Premier League to 10 matches, their longest such streak since going 11 games without a victory between November 1989 and February 1990. nigeria.title: Netanyahu offers to rotate Israeli premiership with Eisenkot
nigeria.description: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday proposed a rotating premiership with his main rival Gadi Eisenkot, who would go first, with the latter expected to announce the formation of a new government within days. Proposing a unity government in a social media post, Netanyahu said “my responsibility as a leader requires me to set everything aside… and agree that Gadi Eisenkot will serve first as prime minister, while I will serve as alternate prime minister at the beginning of the term”. The offer came one day after Eisenkot vowed to announce the formation of Israel’s next government by the official deadline of December 6, without using the option of a 14-day extension. He is expected to form a coalition with anti-Netanyahu parties, but his centrist Yashar party has also been conducting negotiations with Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud. On Friday, however, Eisenkot accused Likud of stalling coalition talks in a bid to bring about new elections. “Likud… has been unwilling to compromise and, over two weeks, refused to put a single concrete proposal on the table,” Eisenkot said in a statement. His wide-ranging camp has faced divisions over whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, the Arab-majority lists, or form a unity government with Likud. Netanyahu opponents scoffed at his offer of a rotating premiership. Youssef Jabareen, leader of the Arab-majority Joint List, which is expected to support an Eisenkot-led government without joining it, wrote: “The democratic majority has decided: this bloodstained, neglectful government must go. It is time to fulfill the shared will of the entire public, Jews and Arabs alike, and remove Netanyahu this (upcoming) week.” “Netanyahu’s proposal is yet another transparent con by a serial fraudster who has deceived every partner and violated every agreement,” wrote former premier Yair Lapid, co-chair of the centrist Beyachad party. Eisenkot’s Yashar party has so far agreed coalition deals with the left-leaning Democrats and the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party. Together, they have a combined total of 36 lawmakers — far short of the 61 needed for a majority in Israel’s 120-seat parliament. Israeli media reported that Mansour Abbas, the leader of the second Arab-Israeli party, Raam, is expected on Saturday to recognise Hamas as a “terror group” — a move that could pave the way for his party to join a possible Eisenkot-led coalition. But some of Eisenkot’s allies have voiced opposition to relying on the support of the Arab-majority lists, which made unprecedented gains in the election. nigeria.title: Ex-Lagos deputy gov, Senator Adebule, dies at 56
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State deputy governor and incumbent senator representing Lagos West senatorial district, Dr. Idiat Oluranti Adebule has died barely 24 hours after celebrating her 56th birthday in the state. Adebule, who was seeking re-election for a second term in the Senate, died in the early hours of Saturday. She was pronounced dead by medical experts at a private hospital in Ikeja, G.R.A., Ikeja Local Government Area of the state, where she was admitted after a brief illness. Adebule was said to be battling an undisclosed ailment for several years before she finally succumbed to death on Saturday. She was the deputy to former Governor Akinwunmi Ambode. The Lagos State All Progressives Congress, APC, spokesman, Seye Oladejo, confirmed the death. He described it as “a rude shock.” He prayed the Almighty God forgive her sins and grant his family, friends, and well-wishers the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss. He, however, announced the postponement of the earlier planned senatorial district for the Lagos West senatorial campaign scheduled for next Monday, November 30. It was learned Senator Adebule was already preparing to attend the campaign rally scheduled for Police College, Ikeja, when the tragedy suddenly occurred. nigeria.title: Man Utd thrashed 4-0 by Brentford in Pochettino’s home debut
nigeria.description: Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 at home by Brentford on Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge to leave the 20-time English champions still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone. Callum Wilson struck a first-half double before late goals from Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade sealed Brentford’s first win at Old Trafford for 89 years on Saturday. Pochettino replaced the sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month, tasked with turning around the fortunes of a club in steep decline. However, the Argentine could barely have imagined a worst start after also losing 4-0 away to Liverpool in his first match in charge last weekend. For the first time in 65 years, United have conceded four goals in three consecutive league matches. That shocking defensive record has plunged the Red Devils into a battle for survival. Only Crystal Palace sit below United and Pochettino’s men could slip to the foot of the table if the Eagles beat Hull on Sunday. Pochettino came out fighting after a series of refereeing decisions went against his side against Liverpool and in a controversial 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday. But there was no hiding place for the new boss or his players after their latest embarrassment. Brentford were missing first-choice striker Igor Thiago through suspension, but it mattered little as his deputy Wilson took advantage of United’s disorganised defence. An encouraging start by the home side was quickly forgotten when Wilson lashed home a brilliant finish to open the scoring on 19 minutes. The former Newcastle and West Ham striker then doubled his tally from Dango Ouattara’s pass 13 minutes later. The end of Carrick’s reign was marked by brief flickers of United resistance in comebacks to beat Roma and salvage a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. Youri Tielemans smashed against the crossbar as United pressed for a route back into the game in the second half. But their inability to defend ended any hope of a fightback as Ajer was given way too much space to fire in from a corner. Schade then completed the rout in stoppage time as Brentford climbed to fifth and within one point of the top four. nigeria.title: 2027 : Atiku, Obi relying on regional support to win election, Shettima says
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Vice President Kashim Shettima has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi of relying on regional support in their bid to win the 2027 presidential election. Shettima made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he questioned the opposition candidates’ campaign strategies and their efforts to build support across the country. He said Obi had visited 17 states, including all five states in the South-East and all South-South states except Rivers, but had made limited visits to other regions. According to Shettima, Obi had visited only Kaduna State in the North and Lagos State in the South-West. He also accused the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate of attempting to use religious divisions to advance his political ambition, insisting that elections could not be won through division. “You cannot win election through divisions. We win elections through negotiation, through compromises, through bridge building,” the Vice-President said. Shettima also criticised Atiku’s campaign activities, claiming that the former vice-president had visited only six states and had not travelled to any state in Southern Nigeria. “My brother Atiku Abubakar, he has so far visited six states in the Federation. He has not visited one state in Southern Nigeria. He has concentrated purely in the North,” he said. The Vice-President argued that presidential candidates needed support beyond their traditional political strongholds to secure victory, citing former President Muhammadu Buhari’s eventual success after building an alliance with the South-West. He said Buhari’s support in the North alone had not been enough to secure the presidency until he formed an alliance with the South-West. Shettima expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would defeat the opposition candidates in the 2027 election. nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) mock accreditation and voting exercise in selected polling units in Kebbi State on Saturday recorded low voter turnout, although the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines operated without reported malfunctions. The exercise witnessed a predominantly female turnout, with relatively few male voters seen at several polling units visited. At Aliero Housing Estate 006 Primary School polling unit, female voters turned out for accreditation, while only a few male voters were sighted. Security personnel, including officers of the Police, Department of State Services (DSS), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and State Security Service (SCIB), were deployed to provide security during the exercise. INEC ad hoc staff at the polling unit confirmed that the BVAS machines were functioning effectively during voter authentication. A visit to Gwadangaji 001 polling unit also showed a low turnout, with a few female voters presenting themselves for accreditation and no male voters sighted at the time. The voters were seen checking their names on the lists displayed on the walls before proceeding with the exercise. However, at Justice Ibrahim Umar polling unit in the GRA NEPA area, a relatively large number of female voters turned out for the mock exercise. The ad hoc staff confirmed that the two BVAS machines provided for the polling unit were working effectively, adding that no malfunction had been recorded since the exercise commenced at 9 a.m. Meanwhile, an APC stakeholder, Alhaji Abubakar ABK, described the exercise as impressive and peaceful. He attributed the participation of female voters to what he described as the humanitarian interventions of Governor Idris, expressing optimism that voters would turn out in large numbers during the January 2027 general elections. ABK urged voters to maintain the peaceful conduct witnessed during the mock exercise when participating in the main elections in 2027. nigeria.title: Tinubu’s reforms push Nigeria’s foreign reserves to $54.13bn – City Boy Movement
nigeria.description: The City Boy Movement has hailed the rise in Nigeria’s gross foreign reserves to $54.13 billion, describing the development as evidence of progress under President Bola Tinubu’s economic reform agenda. The group said the reserves had reached their second-highest level on record since 1999, surpassed only by the $62.08 billion peak recorded in September 2008, when the global financial crisis was unfolding. In a statement titled, “Why Tinubu 4+4? Foreign Reserves Edition,” the movement said Nigeria’s foreign reserves had increased significantly under the Tinubu administration, rising from $32.29 billion in May 2023 to $54.13 billion in November 2026. It put the increase at $21.84 billion, representing nearly 68 per cent growth since the President assumed office. According to the group, the latest figures place Nigeria’s foreign reserves above the peak levels recorded in several years, including 2009, 2007, 2013, 2018, 2025, 2019, 2012 and 2014. The movement noted that Nigeria’s reserves peaked at $53.25 billion in 2009, $51.33 billion in 2007, $48.86 billion in 2013 and $47.87 billion in 2018. It added that the $54.13 billion recorded in 2026 represented the highest level since the 2008 global financial crisis. While acknowledging the difficulties associated with the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, the group argued that the latest reserve figures indicated that the policies were beginning to yield positive results. It said the growth in foreign reserves was an important development in assessing the direction of the economy, expressing optimism that the country was moving towards greater economic prosperity. “The significance is in the history. Even though the reforms have been difficult, the numbers are beginning to tell their own story. We are on the way to prosperity,” the statement said. The movement also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for what it described as progress in the management of the country’s external reserves, reaffirming its support for the President. The figures cited by the group were attributed to data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). However, the movement’s assessment comes amid continuing public debate over the impact of the Federal Government’s economic reforms, particularly their effects on inflation, living costs, businesses and household welfare. While higher foreign reserves can strengthen a country’s capacity to meet external obligations and support confidence in its economy, the extent to which the increase translates into improved living conditions remains a key measure of the overall success of the reforms. business.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Who Phoenix Suns will play in added games from NBA Cup group results
sports.description: The Phoenix Suns will play the Houston Rockets and Oklahoma City Thunder to complete their 82-game schedule after failing to advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals. The Suns (9-9) face the Rockets (14-5) in Houston on Dec. 6 and face the Thunder (10-9) at home Dec. 10. Eight teams are set for the “knockout rounds” after the final group play games on Nov. 27. Dec. 4: East quarterfinal — (3) Philadelphia 76ers at (2) Atlanta Hawks; West quarterfinal — (4) San Antonio Spurs at (1) Dallas Mavericks . Dec. 5: East quarterfinal — (4) Boston Celtics at (1) Detroit Pistons ; West quarterfinal — (3) Memphis Grizzlies at (2) Portland Trail Blazers . The top three seeds won their respective groups, while the fourth seeds are wild cards in their respective conferences. The remaining 22 teams that didn’t advance must play two games amongst themselves to each have a full 82-game regular season. Here’s the NBA’s explanation on how those matchups were decided. “A formulaic approach will determine the matchups for these games using the group play standings in each conference (5th-15th). Two of the 22 games will be scheduled cross-conference since there will be an odd number of teams in each conference that do not advance to the quarterfinals. “These cross-conference games will be scheduled between bottom-finishing teams in the group play stage subject to travel constraints, and no team will play more than one of its two games cross-conference. The other 20 games will be scheduled within conference, featuring teams that are otherwise scheduled to play each other three times over the course of the season wherever possible.” The Suns and Rockets were in West Group A. Phoenix went 1-3 in group play while Houston finished 2-2 with one victory coming against the Suns on Nov. 25. Having already played each other twice this season, they will meet two more times on Dec. 6 and Feb. 5. Phoenix won the first matchup Nov. 7 at home. The teams have recent history that’s factored in intense, heated matchups. Phoenix traded Durant to Houston before the 2025 draft and got Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and the 10 th overall pick in the 2025 draft, 7-footer Khaman Maluach, in return. There were six technical fouls and one flagrant one penalty foul in the last meeting. Brooks was ejected after two technical fouls, with the second coming after he and Durant engaged in a spirited conversation face-to-face late in the game. The Suns and Thunder will now battle each other four times as well this season. Oklahoma City won the first game on Oct. 26. The final three Suns-Thunder matchups will be in Phoenix, as the final two are on a back-to-back March 23-24. Oklahoma City went 2-2 in West Group B. sports.title: Robinson edges Shiffrin to win Killington giant slalom
sports.description: New Zealand's Alice Robinson claimed victory in the women's World Cup giant slalom in Killington, Vermont (Maddie Meyer) Alice Robinson won the women's World Cup giant slalom on Saturday at Killington, where Mikaela Shiffrin settled for second in her return to the Vermont course where she was seriously injured in a 2024 crash. New Zealand's Robinson, second behind Shiffrin after the opening run, defied the poor visibility and deteriorating course conditions to triumph with a total time of 2min 03.02sec, 11-hundredths ahead of Shiffrin. The US superstar held on for second ahead of American teammate Paula Moltzan, who was on the podium again after capturing her first career World Cup win at the season-opening giant slalom in Soelden last month. Robinson, who was 39-hundredths behind Shiffrin after the opening run, bagged her seventh World Cup giant slalom win, her eighth World Cup race victory overall. Shiffrin, meanwhile, remained in search of a first giant slalom win in almost three years. Shiffrin was back at Killington, a two-hour drive from the Burke Mountain Academy she attended as a teenager, for the first time since a 2024 crash that left her with a serious abdominal injury. Shiffrin thrilled her home crowd as she stormed to the lead in the first leg. The 31-year-old American was clearly delighted also, punching a fist in celebration and blowing a kiss to the crowd. Shiffrin had returned to her top form in slalom last season, winning Olympic gold at the Milan-Cortina Winter Games and bagging a sixth overall World Cup title. But she struggled to overcome the psychological toll of her high-speed crash in Killington, in which she suffered a painful deep puncture wound. This year she has opted to focus more on giant slalom and super-G, and Sunday's slalom in Killington will be her first in that discipline this season. bb/nf

sports.title: Quin Snyder, Dyson Daniels explain how Atlanta Hawks turned tables on Boston Celtics
sports.description: For much of the Atlanta Hawks 87-86 NBA Cup win over the Boston Celtics at TD Garden this Friday (Nov. 27) evening, it seemed like Boston's defense was keeping Atlanta from hitting the broad side of a barn with their shot selection. "“I think sometimes if you’re not making shots, it deflates you a little bit, and that’s the right word," said Hawks head coach Quin Snyder. "I think it’s energy and we had a lot more urgency getting the ball in, more urgency running." "But again, sometimes when you’re missing, it’s hard to get back to the present and so even when we got stops, I didn’t think we were quite as urgent to run," he added. "And eventually, something we talked about at halftime, trying to really take advantage of our defense and we never really ended up hitting a lot of shots but we kept shooting and we made some timely ones." "The other thing (was) we weren’t running and we stopped rebounding, but we did defensive rebound," continued the Atlanta coach. Things, however, changed in the third quarter for the Hawks, as Atlanta guard Dyson Daniels noted. "“I just thought everyone sat down and guarded the ball," he recalled. "Our gameplan tonight was to come in, it was going to be a lot less help because of the spacing on the floor. So, let’s sit down and guard the ball, and I thought we did that very well tonight. Everyone came in and really guarded, which was fun." Listen to "Airing Boston Celtics grievances, and feats of strength to fix them" on Spreaker. Calvert-Lewin, who recently signed a new contract , opened the scoring five minutes before half-time, and Longstaff added a second on the stroke of the interval before wrapping up the win midway through the second half. The result lifted Leeds to sixth, while Coventry are just three points above the relegation zone. Coventry boss frustrated by sloppy goals "In recent games we have shown a real competition and energy and today is one where we fell below that and Leeds were on it and are a very good team," Lampard continued. He added: "Both goals [in the first half] were disappointing from our point of view, you can't allow Dominic Calvert-Lewin the freedom to stroll in like that. To come here and get on top is not easy. It's disappointing but I know how much the boys are giving. Leeds have been in this league for a couple of years and are in a different phase." Away form a growing concern The defeat was a painful return to Elland Road for Lampard, whose Derby side famously knocked Leeds out of the Championship play-off semi-finals in 2019 after the Spygate scandal. Coventry have now won just one of their six away league games this season, against Nottingham Forest. However, Lampard insisted the setback would not derail the newly promoted side. "These games can happen, will they define our season? No. But the reaction in games coming up is important and it's important we learn from it," he said. Ipswich clash now crucial Coventry return to the CBS Arena on Tuesday to face Ipswich, and Lampard knows the importance of that fixture. "The next one against Ipswich, those are the games that will define our season," he said.

sports.title: Why your range game doesn't translate to the course
sports.description: Hitting the same club at the same target feels great, but it rarely holds up. Getty Images You take a lesson on a Tuesday afternoon. With your coach watching, your swing feels smooth and crisp, and you hit 40 pure iron shots in a row. You walk off the practice tee convinced you’ve finally figured out this game. On Saturday morning, you stand on the first tee of your club tournament. There’s a pond down the right side and a group watching from behind the tee. You swing and hit a weak push-slice straight into the water. By the 14th hole, you’re searching for whatever swing thought you had on Tuesday. Golfers tell me some version of this story all the time. The problem isn’t talent or mental toughness. It’s that most golfers practice in a way that looks very little like playing golf. On the range, you hit ball after ball with the same club to the same target. On the course, you get one chance with a different club, to a different target, often after a five-minute wait, with real consequences. Why you struggle on the course Motor-learning researchers measure skill development in two ways: retention and transfer. Retention is the ability to reproduce a skill after a break under the same conditions in which you practiced it. Hit crisp 8-irons off a flat mat on Tuesday, come back Thursday and do it again, and you’ve demonstrated retention. Transfer is the ability to take that skill and apply it somewhere new: an uneven lie in the rough, a penalty area down the right, a crosswind and a score that counts. The golf course is the ultimate test of transfer. Yet most golfers spend nearly all their practice time working on retention. Hit the same club to the same target over and over, and the task becomes artificially easy. Your first shot pushes slightly right. On the second, your brain makes a quick adjustment. By the fourth, you’ve started to dial in the timing for that particular club and target. Before long, the shots look effortless. You leave believing you’ve mastered your 8-iron, but what you’ve really done is calibrate your timing through repetition. On the course, you never hit 15 8-irons in a row. You hit a driver, walk for five minutes, find your ball, pull an 8-iron, and face a shot over a bunker. And you get one chance to execute it. When you change clubs and targets with every swing, you can’t rely on the feel of the previous shot. Each ball requires a fresh decision: Read the target, choose the club, visualize the flight and commit. Motor-learning researchers call the added challenge of switching between tasks contextual interference . It tends to make practice look less successful in the moment, but the skills you develop are more likely to hold up when conditions change. sports.title: Man Utd 'reality' tougher than Pochettino expected
sports.description: Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of Manchester United ended in a 4-0 defeat (Darren Staples) Mauricio Pochettino said he could "never expect" to lose his first two Premier League games in charge of Manchester United 4-0 as he urged his players to rise to the "reality" of a relegation battle. Brentford secured their first win at Old Trafford for 89 years on Saturday in a humiliating home debut for Pochettino. United, who sit second bottom of the Premier League, were also thrashed 4-0 away at Liverpool last weekend. At Anfield, Pochettino could at least hide behind a controversial early red card shown to Leny Yoro that forced his side to play for over 80 minutes a man down. There was no such mitigation as Brentford ran riot thanks to Callum Wilson's first-half double before late goals from Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade. "Maybe you say to me: 'tougher than you expect?'. Of course, yes, because we never expect this type of result," said Pochettino. "But that is the reality and we need to accept the reality." United have not been relegated from the English top flight since 1974. But they have won just once in 12 league games this season and could slip to the foot of the table on Sunday if Crystal Palace beat Hull. "I never am going to justify (the results), that is our responsibility. We accept the challenge and we are here and accept that we need to keep pushing, keep working and lifting the players," added Pochettino. "Still we have time. We need to know our reality... We are Manchester United, but you cannot win only with the badge and with the history. "We need to match the opponent in all the areas and then be much better to win the game." By contrast to United's gloom, Brentford are riding the crest of a wave. Despite enjoying a fraction of the resources of the Red Devils, the Bees are flying high in fifth place and within one point of the top four as they target European football for the first time in the club's history. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. The high cost of building on the moon has led to wide-ranging research on how to make use of the moon's most plentiful resource: the dusty regolith that covers its surface. Right now, lunar shipping runs about $544,000 per pound ($1.2 million per kilogram), so anything that astronauts can make on the moon using existing materials could help a lot. Scientists have already proposed using regolith for building 3D-printed bricks , solar arrays , and even as soil to grow potatoes . Now, a team of researchers from Purdue University in Indiana have developed an aerogel made from simulated regolith for insulating lunar habitats. New aerogels created by Purdue University researchers, made of cellulose and lunar regolith simulant, could pave the way for insulating materials made on the moon. (Image credit: Purdue University photo/John Underwood) "Sustaining a long-term presence on the moon will require us to rethink how we use local resources," Wei, professor in Purdue's James Tarpo Jr. and Margaret Tarpo Department of Chemistry, said in a Nov. 19 statement . NASA has said that it wants a long-term, sustainable moon base up and running by 2032, a goal it aims to achieve via its Artemis program . "Rather than relying on Earth to supply everything we need, we're exploring how materials already available on the moon, including waste generated by its inhabitants, could be upcycled into something essential for safe and livable habitats," Wei said. The aerogel that the Purdue researchers have been working on is a mix of fiber from cardboard waste, called cellulose, and a material that simulates regolith. They said that it could protect the people living in habitats from the moon's drastic temperature swings. "Imagine an aerogel as a high-tech thermos for a lunar base," Jacob Staker, a graduate researcher working on the study, said in the same statement. "Most of it consists of empty space that insulates the interior, helping it maintain the temperature of what's inside." The idea here is not to create the best aerogel possible, Wei said, but that "we're looking for the sweet spot where we can get the properties we need with the limited resources we have available" on the moon. The research was published in September in the journal ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 28, 1967: Astronomers Jocelyn Bell and Antony Hewish disover the 1st pulsar with Little Green Men 1 signal
science.description: null On November 28, 1967, astronomers found the first pulsar. A pulsar is a super-dense star that rotates super fast. As the pulsar spins, it emits two beams of light in opposite directions. When astronomers look at a pulsar, it looks like a star that's flickering on and off at a steady, constant pace. The first pulsar was observed by Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish. They were looking at the constellation Vulpecula when they saw a star flickering with regular pulses separated by 1.33 seconds. At first they had no idea what it was, so they jokingly nicknamed the signal Little Green Men 1. After more pulsars were discovered, they were able to rule out aliens. This chart tracked the signal of the first pulsar ever discoverered on Nov. 28, 1967. (Image credit: Cambridge University Library/Wikipedia) Why it mattered Pulsars are naturally occurring phenomena, and they can be handy tools for astronomers . For example, some pulsars are extremely accurate clocks. Because pulsars rotate, their emission of beams of radiation is observed at regular intervals. Until Burnell's discovery, astronomers did not know if neutron stars existed, let alone if they could be observed. "Suddenly, it turned out that nature has provided an incredibly precise way to observe these objects, something that has led to many later advances," said Edward Witten, chairman of the selection committee for the Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize, which in 2018 was awarded to Burnell . Among other applications, the observation of pulsars are one of the best ways astronomers have for testing Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity. The spinning stars have also been used as a navigation tool for spacecraft moving out beyond low Earth orbit. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

"For our 100th parade, we're creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country," said Sharon Otterman, Macy's chief marketing officer, in a statement . First held in 1924 for Macy's colleagues, their friends and families, the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held every year with the exception of a three-year break during World War II. Spanning longer than the dawn of the Space Age, the space race and NASA's entire 68-year history, the celebration has integrated space themes into its displays, even before the first rocket flew beyond Earth's atmosphere . science.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
science.description: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.
